learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling the learning of new methods and technologies, and providing great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer's activity.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunications.

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary group and in a multilingual environment and to communicate, both in writing and orally, knowledge, procedures, results and ideas related to telecommunications and electronics.
Ability to autonomously learn new knowledge and techniques.
Ability to use communication and computer applications to support the development and exploitation of telecommunication networks, services and applications.
Ability to use computer tools for searching bibliographical resources related to telecommunications and electronics.
Ability to understand the mechanisms of propagation and transmission of electromagnetic and acoustic waves, and their corresponding transmitting and receiving devices.
Establish the equations of electromagnetic theory for modeling wave propagation and radiation.
Obtain and manage the canonical solutions of propagation: plane, cylindrical and spherical wave.
Specify the characteristics and parameters of electromagnetic propagation as a function of the transmission medium.
Analyze the effects of reflection and transmission of electromagnetic waves and interpret their behavior.
Establish the equations for modeling the generation and propagation of acoustic waves.
Analyze the effects of reflection and transmission of acoustic waves and interpret their behavior.
Analyze the propagation modes in a guided system.

assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as 0.13*P1 + 0.13*P2 + 0.04*P3 + 0.7*EX. The extraordinary call consists of a single exam evaluating all course content, and the grade will be that obtained in this exam. Students who cannot participate in the described evaluation process must request differentiated evaluation, adapting the procedure according to university regulations. The teaching staff may request a face-to-face defense of any assessable test if there are doubts about authorship or the use of unauthorized means.
